ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Persistent mitochondrial failure after reperfusion

In an experiment, ischemic cells are reoxygenated and supplied with glucose. One group recovers, while another has persistent mitochondrial dysfunction and extensive membrane damage despite restored conditions. Which interpretation best describes the second group?

  1. The injury has crossed into an irreversible state
  2. All changes are necessarily reversible because oxygen returned
  3. The cells have undergone physiologic hypertrophy
  4. The findings establish an exclusively apoptotic mechanism
  5. ATP depletion never contributed to the injury
Answer and explanation

The injury has crossed into an irreversible state

Persistent inability to restore mitochondrial function with severe membrane damage supports irreversible injury.

Option explanations

The injury has crossed into an irreversible state: Persistent inability to restore mitochondrial function with severe membrane damage supports irreversible injury.

All changes are necessarily reversible because oxygen returned: Restoring the environment cannot rescue cells that have passed the irreversible threshold.

The cells have undergone physiologic hypertrophy: Hypertrophy is adaptive growth rather than failure of viability.

The findings establish an exclusively apoptotic mechanism: Severe membrane damage is compatible with necrosis and does not establish apoptosis alone.

ATP depletion never contributed to the injury: Earlier ATP depletion can initiate the cascade leading to irreversible damage.
